evidence: Plaut. Trin. 4.2.136: quid id ad mē attinet? (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Poen. 3.3.24: Quid istuc ad mē attinet? (Lewis & Short s.v. attineō)
Traupman 285: quid id ad tē attinet?
terms.comment: Attinet ad mē, it concerns me, is the usual classical sense of the verb (Lewis & Short). What business is it of yours? Quid id ad tē attinet? (Traupman 94).

terms.gloss: that’s his business: let him see to it
evidence: M-O s.v. business: that’s his business

terms.comment: After Terence’s aliēna ut cūrēs. Minding one’s own is sua negōtia cūrāre (Traupman 104); I always mind my own business, meum negōtium agō semper (Traupman 94).

phrases.latin: tantumne est ab rē tuā ōtī tibi, aliēna ut cūrēs, eaque nihil quae ad tē attinent?
phrases.english: have you so much time to spare from your own affairs that you mind other people’s, things that are none of your business?
It’s my business to see what’s going on.
I always mind my own business.
